items.evidence: Vanilla 1.21.10 registers ELDER_GUARDIAN (SimpleParticleType, wire id 17, overrideLimiter=true — parsed fresh from the 1.21.10 ParticleTypes <clinit>) with a dedicated ElderGuardianParticle$Provider (ParticleResources.registerProviders, offsets 296-300) and spawns it on game event GUARDIAN_ELDER_EFFECT (ClientPacketListener.handleGameEvent, offset 544; addParticle at the player position, offset 554, plus the curse sound at 598 — all re-read from the 1.21.10 client jar). The port's ParticleType enum (125 variants) lacks it, so received_particle drops server-sent elder_guardian packets (lan_particles.rs:488), /particle rejects it (particle.notFound, world_cmds.rs:718), and override_limiter() misses it (28 vanilla vs 27 real-1.21.10 Rust entries; the Rust list's 4 extra entries are the dead geyser types). The providers driver does NOT send elder_guardian cases (omitted from the 126-kind set), so the defect blocks no driver here — it silently skips the type. The in-game curse apparition IS re-implemented via game event 10 + elder_apparition_geometry (30-tick lifetime, mob_blocks.rs:87/96), so the main visible path works through a different mechanism (fidelity unverified).
items.title: elder_guardian has no port implementation at all: no ParticleType variant, no engine provider, no limiter entry (recurs from 1.21.7; reproduces from 26.1.2)

items.evidence: Particle::read decodes wire id 42 (flash, verified against the 1.21.10 registry — id 41 in 1.21.7, 42 here) as Color(i32) — a flash particle always carries a colour — but hub_particle has no Flash arm in its Color match (EntityEffect | TintedLeaves only, lan_particles.rs:437), so the packet is built with data None and Particle::write (writes data by presence, not id) emits the id with no colour bytes; guests reading id 42 consume the next 4 stream bytes as the colour and desync. Reachable only via /particle flash on a LAN host (cmd_particle builds ParticleOptions::simple(ty) via the catch-all, world_cmds.rs:829; Flash is otherwise created client-side only, in firework explosions, particles.rs:3785); the local player draws directly and is unaffected.

items.evidence: Vanilla 1.21.10 has no SpeleothemBlock class at all (0 entries in either jar; PointedDripstoneBlock extends Block directly) and no speleothems tag in either jar's datapack. Vanilla LevelEventHandler routes 1504 to PointedDripstoneBlock.spawnDripParticle with no class gate (offset 3519, verified fresh). The client routes 1504 to dripstone_drip_particle (game.rs:4388), whose first act is the is_stalactite gate (level_particles.rs:243-244): has_class("SpeleothemBlock") is false for every block in 1.21.10, so the drip particle never spawns. The ambient animateTick drip path is unaffected (name-based table, animate_tick.rs:397-410; 0.12 roll, same-block climb, 0.02 cauldron rule all match vanilla). Whether the port's server actually transfers fluid to cauldrons in 1.21.10 (G6's status) is Batch 5's scope; the client gate is dead regardless.

items.evidence: Vanilla 1.21.10's ParticleGroup.add is a plain queue add into an EvictingQueue.create(16384) (javap -c on the 1.21.10 client jar: particles.add(p); the queue itself is an EvictingQueue, constructor offsets 5-8) — when the queue is full the OLDEST particle is evicted to make room for the new one. There is no size check and no probability roll in add; the cap is enforced by eviction, not rejection. The 1.21.10 port's tick_tracking (particles.rs:3888, the drain that moves every created particle from pending into the live list — create() pushes to pending, :2098) enforces the 26.2 form (:3933-3945): at 16,384 live particles every new particle is dropped, and above 12,288 new particles are dropped with probability 1 - ((16384-size)/4096)^2, drawing the level random for each rejection (constant at :1358-1359). The port's behaviour matches neither vanilla 1.21.10 (evict oldest) nor vanilla 26.1.2 (plain queue, no cap at all). The cap only bites in particle-heavy scenes (above 12,288 live particles); below that threshold the port matches vanilla exactly. The repair here is evict-oldest, not the 26.1 tree's cap removal.
items.title: Particle engine drops new particles at the 16,384 cap (with probabilistic thinning above 12,288); vanilla 1.21.10 evicts the oldest instead

items.evidence: Vanilla 1.21.10's TeleportRandomlyConsumeEffect is a record with ONE field (diameter: float) — no directional_particles field — and its apply calls LivingEntity.randomTeleport(x, y, z, true), which broadcasts entity event 46 (128 portal particles at the entity; LivingEntity.handleEntityEvent case 46, offsets 193/381/399; broadcast at bipush 46, offset 177). Vanilla LevelEventHandler has NO 2017 case (79-case lookupswitch). The 1.21.10 tree carries the 26.3 form: TeleportConsume has a directional_particles: bool field (teleport_consume.rs:6); items.rs:157-160 reads it from data with unwrap_or(true), and the 1.21.10 data never carries the field (chorus_fruit consumable is {"on_consume_effects": [{"type": "minecraft:teleport_randomly"}]}; 0 occurrences of directional_particles in the datagen items.json), so it defaults to true; teleport_consume.rs:109-121 fires the event on every successful teleport and the client impl (consume.rs:422-431) calls level_event_at(2017, ...), routed (game.rs:4349-4352) to consume_teleport_particles -> block_teleportation ([127,127,127], particles.rs:1859), 128 portal particles along the old->new line. The port ALSO fires the vanilla-correct event 46 (consume.rs:188-194, remote.rs:4774-4777), so a chorus-fruit teleport shows BOTH the correct burst AND a second, wrong directional trail. The 26.1 tree has no directional_particles anywhere.
items.title: Chorus fruit shows an extra 2017 directional teleport trail vanilla never sends, on top of the correct event-46 burst (26.3-form; the 26.1 tree has no such event)

items.evidence: Vanilla 1.21.10's MultiPlayerGameMode never calls addBreakingBlockEffect anywhere in the class (0 occurrences in the full javap -c dump), and LevelEventHandler has NO 2019/2020 cases. startDestroyBlock plays nothing and spawns nothing; continueDestroyBlock plays ONLY the hit sound, on destroy ticks 0, 4, 8, ... (destroyTicks % 4.0 == 0, volume (volume+1)/8, pitch * 0.5, offsets 199-208) — no particle at any point while digging. The 1.21.10 tree keeps the 26.2 form: breaking_block_effects (level_particles.rs:353-373: hit sound when play_sound, plus crack_particle — one crumb on the mined face), called from startDestroyBlock (remote.rs:8172, breaking_block_effects(hit.pos, hit.face, true)). The 26.1 tree is correct here (start plays nothing; continue plays sound-only on ticks 1, 5, 9, ...). The particle half (extra crumb) is minted here; the sound-schedule half is flagged for Batch 10.

items.evidence: Batch 7-routed flag, verified fresh here. Vanilla 1.21.10's SpreadPlayersCommand.Position.isSafe (javap -c, 1.21.10 server-game jar) is y < maxY && !state.liquid() && !state.is(BlockTags.FIRE) — no teleport tag. The #entities_can_teleport_to tag does not exist in 1.21.10: 0 entries in either jar's datapack (verified by jar listing; the tag is a 26.2 addition). The port's spread_safe (world_cmds.rs:2091-2114) returns y < max_y && !liquid && teleportable, where teleportable (:2100-2109) requires membership in #entities_can_teleport_to — always false in 1.21.10. So spread_safe is ALWAYS false; in the spread loop (:1978-1986) every collision-free iteration re-randomizes every point, collisions stays true, and the loop runs until iteration >= 10_000, when the command fails with commands.spreadplayers.failed.entities (or .teams, :1991-1999). /spreadplayers cannot succeed in the 1.21.10 port on any terrain. Commands-area; minted here on the coordinator's routing via Batch 7 — the merge may re-route it to Batch 9's ledger.
items.method: javap + data + source (Batch 7-routed flag, verified fresh)
items.title: /spreadplayers always fails: spread_safe requires the #entities_can_teleport_to tag, which 1.21.10 does not have (Batch 7-routed; reproduces from 26.1.2)

systemic_note: Same shape as the 26.1.2 batch, with two 1.21.10 twists. First, the 1.21.10 tree inherits the 26.1.2 tree's particle defects exactly by template: the four reproduced original defects are four different shapes (a missing registry entry carried through every table (B8-G01), a write-path/read-path asymmetry in one codec arm (B8-G02), a wrong per-block belief baked into both the port and the driver's own comment (B8-G03), and a 26.2+-only class name gating a 1.21.10 path (B8-G04)), and the five 26.2/26.3-form reversions (B8-G05–G09) carry over unchanged. But B8-G05 is a different defect here: vanilla 1.21.10 caps by eviction (EvictingQueue), not by rejection and not by no-cap, so the repair is evict-oldest, not the 26.1 tree's cap removal. Second, the oracle problem is bigger: 7 of 8 particle oracles fail to compile for 1.21.10 (92 errors total) because the oracle sources are 26.3-form — 26.x packages, jspecify, 26.x constructor forms — and 1.21.10 predates all of them. The directional-teleport events are one feature in three defects: 2017/2018 ADD a trail on top of the correct event-46 burst (double particles), while 2016 is pure invention (vanilla shows no particles for a shulker teleport at all). The sixth carried defect (B8-G10, /spreadplayers) is the opposite shape: code shared verbatim with the 26.1 tree that both runs' Batch 9 missed. The positive systemic finding stands: the port's particle tables are otherwise exact — all 115 types covered end-to-end except elder_guardian, all 18 data-carrying wire ids correct, all 28 limiter flags correct except elder_guardian, all 27 real entity-burst pairs and all 45 marker-zoo blocks covered, and all 11 leaf blocks' chances verified — the gaps are narrow and enumerated, not a broad drift. The 11 extra types in the Rust enum are dead but unreachable.
